readings.title: Joseph’s Dreams
readings.text: [Genesis 37:1] And Ya’aqoḇ dwelt in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Kena’an. [2] This is the genealogy of Ya’aqoḇ: Yosĕph, being seventeen years old, was feeding <dn>את</dn> the flock with his brothers. And the young man was with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives. And Yosĕph brought <dn>את</dn> a limited report of them to his father. [3] And Yisra’ĕl loved <dn>את</dn> Yosĕph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age. And he made him a long robe. [4] And his brothers saw that their father loved <dn>את</dn> him more than all his brothers, and they hated <dn>את</dn> him and were unable to speak peaceably to him. [5] And Yosĕph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated <dn>את</dn> him even more. [6] And he said to them, “Please hear this dream which I have dreamed: [7] “See, we were binding sheaves in the midst of the field, and see, my sheaf rose up and also stood upright. And see, your sheaves stood all around and bowed down to my sheaf.” [8] And his brothers said to him, “Shall you indeed reign over us? Shall you indeed rule over us?” So they hated <dn>את</dn> him even more for his dreams and for his words. [9] And he dreamed still another dream and told <dn>את</dn> it to his brothers, and said, “See, I have dreamed another dream, and see, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars bowed down to me.” [10] And he told it to his father and his brothers. And his father rebuked him and said to him, “What is this dream that you have dreamed? Shall we, your mother and my sons and I, indeed come to bow down to the earth before you?” [11] And his brothers were envious of him, but his father kept <dn>את</dn> the matter in mind. [12] And his brothers went to feed <dn>את</dn> their father’s flock in Sheḵem. [13] And Yisra’ĕl said to Yosĕph, “Are not your brothers feeding the flock in Sheḵem? Come, let me send you to them.” And he said to him, “Here I am.” [14] And he said to him, “Please go at once, see <dn>את</dn> if it is well with your brothers and well <dn>את</dn> with the sheep, and bring back word to me.” So he sent him out of the Valley of Heḇron, and he went to Sheḵem. [15] And a certain man found <dn>את</dn> him, and see, he was wandering in the field. And the man asked <dn>את</dn> him, saying, “What are you seeking?” [16] And he said, “I am seeking <dn>את</dn> my brothers. Please tell me where they are feeding their flocks.” [17] And the man said, “They have moved from here, for I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’” So Yosĕph went after his brothers and found <dn>את</dn> them in Dothan.

readings.title: Joseph Sold into Egypt
readings.text: [Genesis 37:18] And they saw <dn>את</dn> him from a distance, and before he came near them, they plotted against him to kill <dn>את</dn> him. [19] And they said to each one another, “See, this master of dreams is coming! [20] “And now, come, let us kill <dn>את</dn> him and cast <dn>את</dn> him into some pit. And we shall say, ‘Some wild beast has devoured him.’ Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams!” [21] And Reḇ'uḇĕn heard and delivered <dn>את</dn> him out of their hands, and said, “Let us not strike his life.” [22] And Reḇ'uḇĕn said to them, “Shed no blood, but cast <dn>את</dn> him into this pit which is in the wilderness, and do not lay a hand on him” – in order to deliver <dn>את</dn> him out of their hands, to bring <dn>את</dn> him back to his father. [23] And it came to be, when Yosĕph had come to his brothers, that they stripped <dn>את</dn> Yosĕph of <dn>את</dn> his robe, <dn>את</dn> the long robe which was on him. [24] And they took <dn>את</dn> him and cast <dn>את</dn> him into a pit. And the pit was empty, there was no water in it. [25] And they sat down to eat a meal. And they lifted their eyes and looked and saw a company of Yishma’ĕlites, coming from Gil’aḏ with their camels, bearing spices and balm and myrrh, going to carry them down to Mitsrayim. [26] And Yehuḏah said to his brothers, “What is the gain if we kill <dn>את</dn> our brother and cover <dn>את</dn> his blood? [27] “Come, let us sell <dn>את</dn> him to the Yishma’ĕlites, and let not our hand be upon him, for he is our brother and our flesh.” And his brothers listened. [28] And Miḏyanite traders passed by, and they pulled <dn>את</dn> Yosĕph up and lifted him out of the pit, and sold <dn>את</dn> Yosĕph to the Yishma’ĕlites for twenty pieces of silver. And they took <dn>את</dn> Yosĕph to Mitsrayim. [29] And Reḇ'uḇĕn returned to the pit, and see, Yosĕph was not in the pit. And he tore <dn>את</dn> his garments. [30] And he returned to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! And I, where am I to go?” [31] So they took <dn>את</dn> Yosĕph’s robe, and killed a male goat, and dipped <dn>את</dn> the robe in the blood. [32] And they sent <dn>את</dn> the long robe, and they brought it to their father and said, “We have found this. Please examine it, whether it is your son’s robe or not.” [33] And he recognized <dn>את</dn> it and said, “It is my son’s robe. A wild beast has devoured him. Yosĕph is without doubt torn to pieces.” [34] And Ya’aqoḇ tore <dn>את</dn> his garments, and put sackcloth on his waist, and mourned for his son many days. [35] And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted, and he said, “For I go down into the grave to my son in mourning.” So his father wept for him. [36] And the Miḏyanites sold <dn>את</dn> him in Mitsrayim to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.

readings.title: Judah and Tamar
readings.text: [Genesis 38:1] And it came to be at that time that Yehuḏah went down from his brothers, and turned in to a certain Aḏullamite whose name was Ḥirah. [2] And Yehuḏah saw there a daughter of a certain Kena’anite whose name was Shuwa, and he took <dn>את</dn> her and went in to her. [3] And she conceived and bore a son, and he called <dn>את</dn> his name Ěr. [4] And she conceived again and bore a son, and she called <dn>את</dn> his name Onan. [5] And she conceived yet again and bore a son, and called <dn>את</dn> his name Shĕlah. Now he was at Kĕziḇ when she bore him. [6] And Yehuḏah took a wife for Ěr his first-born, and her name was Tamar. [7] But Ěr, Yehuḏah’s first-born, was evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> killed <dn>את</dn> him. [8] And Yehuḏah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her, and raise up seed for your brother.” [9] But Onan knew that the seed should not be his. And it came to be, when he went in to his brother’s wife, that he let it go on the ground, so as not to give seed to his brother. [10] And that which he did was evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so <dn>He</dn> killed <dn>את</dn> him also. [11] Then Yehuḏah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father’s house until my son Shĕlah is grown.” For he said, “Lest he also die like his brothers.” And Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house. [12] And in the course of time the daughter of Shuwa, Yehuḏah’s wife, died. And Yehuḏah was comforted, and went up to his sheep-shearers at Timnah, he and his friend Ḥirah the Aḏullamite. [13] And it was told Tamar, saying, “See, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.” [14] So she took off her widow’s garments, and covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place which was on the way to Timnah. For she saw that Shĕlah was grown, and she was not given to him as a wife. [15] And Yehuḏah saw <dn>את</dn> her and thought she was a harlot, because she had covered her face. [16] And he turned to her by the way, and said, “Please come, let me come in to you,” for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What do you give me, that you might come in to me?” [17] And he said, “I send a young goat from the flock.” And she said, “If you give a pledge until you send it.” [18] And he said, “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said, “Your signet and your cord, and your staff that is in your hand.” And he gave them to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him. [19] And she rose up and went away, and took off her veil from her and put on the garments of her widowhood. [20] And Yehuḏah sent <dn>את</dn> the young goat by the hand of his friend the Aḏullamite, to receive <dn>את</dn> the pledge from the woman’s hand, but he did not find <dn>את</dn> her. [21] And he asked the men of that place, saying, “Where is the harlot who was at the open place by the wayside?” And they said, “There was no harlot in this place.” [22] And he returned to Yehuḏah and said, “I have not found <dn>את</dn> her. And the men of the place also said, ‘There was no harlot in this place.’” [23] And Yehuḏah said, “Let her take them for herself, lest we become a laughing-stock. See, I sent <dn>את</dn> this young goat and you have not found <dn>את</dn> her.” [24] And it came to be, about three months later, that Yehuḏah was told, saying, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has committed harlotry, and see, she is even pregnant by harlotry.” And Yehuḏah said, “Bring her out and let her be burned!” [25] When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “By the man to whom these belong, I am pregnant.” And she said, “Please examine, whose are these – the signet and cord and staff?” [26] And Yehuḏah recognized them and said, “She is more righteous than I, because I did not give her to Shĕlah my son.” And he never knew her again. [27] And it came to be, in the time of her giving birth, that see, twins were in her womb. [28] And it came to be, when she was giving birth, that the one put out his hand. And the midwife took a scarlet thread and bound it on his hand, saying, “This one came out first.” [29] And it came to be, as he drew back his hand, that see, his brother came out! And she said, “How you have broken through! On you be the breach!” So his name was called Perets. [30] And afterward his brother came out who had the scarlet thread on his hand. And his name was called Zeraḥ.

readings.title: The Genealogy of Judah
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 2:3] The sons of Yehuḏah: Ěr, and Onan, and Shĕlah. These three were born to him by the daughter of Shuwa, the Kena’anitess. And Ěr, the first-born of Yehuḏah, was evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> killed <dn>את</dn> him. [4] And Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him <dn>את</dn> Perets and <dn>את</dn> Zeraḥ. All the sons of Yehuḏah were five. [5] The sons of Perets: Ḥetsron and Hamul. [6] The sons of Zeraḥ: Zimri, and Ěthan, and Hĕman, and Kalkol, and Dara – five of them in all. [8] And the son of Ěthan: Azaryah.

readings.title: Joseph in Potiphar’s House
readings.text: [Genesis 39:1] And Yosĕph had been taken down to Mitsrayim. And Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, a Mitsrite, bought <dn>את</dn> him from the Yishma’ĕlites who had taken <dn>את</dn> him down there. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was <dn>את</dn> with Yosĕph, and he became a prosperous man. And he was in the house of his master the Mitsrite. [3] And his master saw that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was <dn>את</dn> with him and that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made <dn>את</dn> all he did to prosper in his hand. [4] So Yosĕph found favour in his eyes, and attended <dn>את</dn> him. And he appointed him overseer over his house, and <dn>את</dn> all that he had he put into his hand. [5] And it came to be, from the time that he had appointed <dn>את</dn> him overseer in his house and over all that he had, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrite’s house for Yosĕph’s sake. And the blessing of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was on all that he had in the house and in the field. [6] And he left all that he had in Yosĕph’s hand, and with <dn>את</dn> him he knew naught except the bread which he ate. And Yosĕph was handsome in form and handsome in appearance. [7] And it came to be after these matters that his master’s wife lifted her eyes toward Yosĕph, and said, “Lie with me.” [8] But he refused and said to his master’s wife, “See, my master does not know what is with me in the house, and he has put <dn>את</dn> all that he has into my hand. [9] “No one is greater in this house than I, and he has not withheld whatever from me, except you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great evil, and sin against <dn>Elohim</dn>?” [10] And it came to be, as she spoke to Yosĕph day by day, that he did not listen to her, to lie beside her or to be with her. [11] And it came to be about this time, that he went into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the house was there in the house. [12] And she caught <dn>את</dn> him by his garment, saying, “Lie with me.” But he left his garment in her hand, and fled and went outside. [13] And it came to be, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside, [14] that she called to the men of her house and spoke to them, saying, “See, he has brought in to us a Heḇrew to mock us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice. [15] “And it came to be, when he heard that I lifted my voice and cried out, that he left his garment with me, and fled and went outside.” [16] And she kept his garment beside her until his master came home. [17] And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, “The Heḇrew servant whom you brought to us came in to me to mock me. [18] “And it came to be, as I lifted my voice and cried out, that he left his garment with me and fled outside.”

readings.title: Joseph in Prison
readings.text: [Genesis 39:19] And it came to be, when his master heard <dn>את</dn> the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, “According to these words your servant did to me,” that his wrath burned. [20] And Yosĕph’s master took <dn>את</dn> him and put <dn>את</dn> him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were confined. And he was there in the prison. [21] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was <dn>את</dn> with Yosĕph and extended kindness to him, and <dn>He</dn> gave him favour in the eyes of the warden of the prison. [22] And the warden of the prison delivered into Yosĕph’s hand <dn>את</dn> all the prisoners who were in the prison, and whatever was done there, it was he who did it. [23] The warden of the prison did not look into <dn>את</dn> whatever was in his hand, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was <dn>את</dn> with him. And whatever he did, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made it to prosper.
